module: Engine of the editor's Resource Checker tool: analyzes the materials, textures, meshes and assets of a level or vehicle (material versions, duplicates, persistentId, missing or non-power-of-two textures, unused materials/models/textures, dummies, colmeshes, DDS to PNG export, size statistics). Each check runs in a job (extensions.core_jobsystem.create) that updates a progress value and returns its result to the UI via extensions.editor_resourceChecker.jobData(channel, {type, count, ..., isDone}). Several functions modify or delete files (fixPID, removeDummy, removeUnused, textureExporter): use with caution.
usage:
local ru = extensions.editor_resourceChecker_resourceUtil
ru.verifyVersion('/levels/mon_niveau/')
-- later, in the UI:
local p = ru.getProgress()
if p then print(p) end -- 0..100, nil if no job is running
notes: The check functions return nothing: the result arrives asynchronously via extensions.editor_resourceChecker.jobData(...). This module therefore depends on the editor_resourceChecker extension.
isDone is 1 on success and 2 on error (invalid path or missing level name) in the returned data.
Material paths must contain a "/" otherwise the function logs an error (ensureValidPath).

The exported xxxworkJob fields are nil when the module loads (copy of local variables not yet assigned): the jobs themselves are private locals, getProgress and stopProgress are the only reliable interface.
removeUnusedworkJob is not exported, but getProgress/stopProgress handle it. checkColData accepts a removal parameter that is not passed to the job (inferred from code).
textureExporter: the log('E'/'I', 'text') calls pass the message as the tag (two-argument call with a single message); if convertDDSToPNG fails, the file is still counted and listed.
The functions that parse material files handle materials.cs (TorqueScript, home-made parser) and *materials.json.

matstoRemove.desc: List of unused materials found by checkUnusedMats; replaced by M.matstoRemove at the end of the job. Then used by removeUnused (item 1).

shapestoRemove.desc: List of unused models (shapes) found by checkUnusedModels; used by removeUnused (item 2).

textoRemove.desc: List of unused textures found by unusedTextures; used by removeUnused (item 3).

checkUnusedMatsworkJob.desc: Exported but nil (see notes): handle of the checkUnusedMats job.

checkUsedMatsworkJob.desc: Exported but nil (see notes): handle of the checkUsedMats job.

checkUnusedModelsworkJob.desc: Exported but nil (see notes): handle of the checkUnusedModels job.

unusedTexturesworkJob.desc: Exported but nil (see notes): handle of the unusedTextures job.

checkColDataworkJob.desc: Exported but nil (see notes): handle of the checkColData job.

duplicateDataworkJob.desc: Exported but nil (see notes): handle of the duplicateData job.

removeDummyworkJob.desc: Exported but nil (see notes): handle of the removeDummy job.

textureExporterworkJob.desc: Exported but nil (see notes): handle of the textureExporter job.

getSimObjects.desc: Walks through all scene objects (scenetree.getAllObjects) and returns those whose getFileName() equals the given file. Used to find the objects created by loading a materials file.

fileName.desc: Path of the object's source file (e.g. a materials.json).

resaveMaterial.desc: Reloads a materials.json file, clears the persistentId of each Material then saves it via a temporary PersistenceManager. Rewrites the file.

file.desc: Path of an existing materials file.

powerOfTwo.desc: Tests whether a number is a power of two (useful for texture dimensions).

returns.desc: false if x is nil or <= 0 or is not a power of two.

removeFromForestJson.desc: Opens a ForestItemData JSON file, removes the entry whose shapeFile matches shape and rewrites the file. Logs a warning if not found.

foresData.desc: Path of the forest JSON file.

getMaterialTexFields.desc: For a Material object, returns its non-empty filename-type fields, per layer (4 layers for version 0 or 1, activeLayers for 1.5, otherwise 1).

returns.desc: "field.layer" keys to file path; nil (and E log) if it is not a Material.

findDuplicates.desc: Detects duplicate material names and duplicate mapTo (excluding unmapped_mat) in a list. The result is stored in an internal module state used by verifyDuplicate.

verifyVersion.desc: Job: counts the materials of version < 1.5 (old) and those at 1.5 (PBR) under a folder, and lists the old ones with their file. Actually loads the material files into the game. Result via jobData(2, {2, nbOld, list, nbPBR, isDone}).

verifyDuplicate.desc: Job: finds materials whose name or mapTo is duplicated. With skipCommon == false, includes /vehicles/common, /art and /core. Result via jobData(2, {3, count, "dummy", list, isDone}).

skipCommon.desc: false to include the common folders.

fixPID.desc: Job: removes persistentIds from JSON materials by re-saving them (resaveMaterial). Modifies files. Result via jobData(2, {5, count, "", modifiedFiles, isDone}).

skipCommon.desc: false to include the common folders.

checkMatTex.desc: Job: checks the textures referenced by the materials (missing files, incorrect paths). Result via jobData(2, {6, ...}).

checkTex.desc: Job: checks the texture files themselves (e.g. power-of-two dimensions, see powerOfTwo). Result via jobData(2, {7, ...}).

checkmissingMats.desc: Job: looks in the meshes for materials that are referenced but absent from the material files. Result via jobData(2, {8, ...}).

checkStatic.desc: Job: lists the shapes used by the scene's TSStatics. Result via jobData(3, {1, ...}).

checkForest.desc: Job: lists the scene's ForestItemData. Result via jobData(3, {2, ...}).

checkTerrains.desc: Job: lists the scene's TerrainBlocks. Result via jobData(3, {3, ...}).

checkUnusedMats.desc: Job: determines which of a level's materials are not used by any object (prefabs, forest, TSStatic, terrains, GroundPlane, GroundCover, DecalRoad, MeshRoad, DecalData). Stores the result in matstoRemove. jobData(3, {4, ...}).

checkUsedMats.desc: Job: same traversal as checkUnusedMats but to list the used materials. jobData(3, {8, ...}).

checkColData.desc: Job: looks for the colmeshes (collision) used in a level (prefabs, forest, TSStatic). jobData(3, {9, ...}).

removal.desc: Not passed to the job (see notes).

checkUnusedModels.desc: Job: finds the level's unused models (shapes) (prefabs, TSStatic, forest, GroundCover). Stores the result in shapestoRemove. jobData(3, {5, ...}).

unusedTextures.desc: Job: finds the unreferenced textures (materials, TerrainMaterials, WaterPlane/Block, River, CloudLayer, ScatterSky, Cubemap, Info). Stores the result in textoRemove. jobData(3, {6, ...}).

removeUnused.desc: Job: deletes the selected unused items. item 1 removes materials (matstoRemove), 2 shapes (shapestoRemove, and forest entries), 3 textures (textoRemove). Deletes files: irreversible. jobData(3, {7, ...}).

selected.desc: Table whose keys are the selected entries to delete.

duplicateData.desc: Job: walks through the materials in /levels, /vehicles, /art and /core to find duplicates of a given material.

material.desc: Material to search for; E log if nil.

removeDummy.desc: Job: removes "dummy" materials (without Stages or with empty Stages[1]) from the materials.json files and rewrites the files. jobData(2, {9, count, "dummy", list, isDone}).

skipCommon.desc: false to include the common folders.

textureExporter.desc: Job: converts the .dds files found under a folder to .png (convertDDSToPNG) for those that do not already have a .png, writing under exportpath. jobData(2, {10, count, "dummy", files, isDone}).

exportpath.desc: Prefix of the PNG output path (concatenated with the folder and the name).

assetStats.desc: Job: computes size statistics of a level's assets (textures, source and cached meshes, terrains, audio, datablocks, others) and the list of files with their size. jobData(3, {typeId, breakdown, totals, sceneCounts, isDone, {files = ...}}).

getProgress.desc: Returns the progress of the current job (among all the module's jobs), or nil if none is running.

stopProgress.desc: Requests all running jobs to stop by setting job.stop = true; the jobs stop at their next checkpoint (abort).
